purpose: Replace the sequence-wide appearance-complexity test with a phase-aware sensor-integrity test so a physically real body-fixed-camera fall is not censored for showing a dark or low-texture nearby floor. This development replay cannot relabel any sealed v4/v5 batch.

diagnosis.old_gate_problem: The old both_sequences_visually_valid check applied a scene-level appearance-complexity threshold to every post-effect frame. It therefore conflated renderer or sensor failure with legitimate low-texture close-floor content caused by O4-induced pitch or fall.
diagnosis.statistical_risk: Conditioning benchmark admission on visually complex post-failure frames creates outcome-dependent censoring and can preferentially remove the strongest physical failures.
preserved_contracts: strict multi-view RTX scene admission remains unchanged
all source, corridor, articulated-Go2, operator, paired consequence, ordering, and terminal-outcome checks remain unchanged
all RGB files and manifests remain hash-verified

pre_effect_context.scope: all nominal and O4 frames at or before first attachment

sensor_integrity.scope: all captured nominal and O4 frames, including registered terminal fall

frozen_visual_contract.terminal_binding: When O4 falls, the last captured RGB frame must equal the registered first_fall_step and pass sensor integrity.
frozen_visual_contract.overall_rule: Every inherited nonvisual check and every phase-aware visual check must pass.

decision_rule.admit_for_new_heldout_batch: All four positive controls pass v6, both physical negative controls remain failed specifically because inherited nonvisual checks fail, all artifacts match their hashes, and unit plus regression tests pass.

authorized_inference: The phase-aware visual contract is development-supported for a new preregistered held-out batch; it is not yet confirmatory evidence and does not make O4 or Kino-Fail publication-ready by itself.
